result:
The proposed answer (61, 68) is almost certainly wrong, and the solution gives no derivation or source for it.

I could not recall the published counts, so this rests on a rough check of the rod-group side. Many rod groups collapse to the same abstract group. Rod groups with a single screw axis, such as 1, 2₁, 3₁, 3₂, 4₁, 4₂, 4₃, 6₁ through 6₅, and the pure translation groups, are all abstractly isomorphic to ℤ. Enantiomorphic pairs also become isomorphic, for example 4₁ and 4₃, or 6₁ and 6₅. Groups that differ only in whether an operation is a glide or a reflection, or a screw or a rotation, also coincide as abstract groups.

These coincidences account for far more than the 14 merges that going from 75 to 61 would allow. The true rod-group count should be much smaller than 61, probably around 30. The layer-group count of 68 is also doubtful for similar reasons.

VERDICT: REJECT
